definitions.text: A plane figure which is formed by two rays sharing a common end point is called an angle. The two rays are known as the sides of the angle. The common end point is known as vertex. The amount of rotation or measure of opening between these rays is called an angle.

The angle is said to be in standard position if:
(a) Its vertex is located at the origin of the coordinate plane.
(b) One of its rays (the initial side) lies along the positive x-axis.
Co-terminal angles are angles that share the same initial side and terminal side in standard position, but they may have different measures. These angles differ by a multiple of 360° or 2π rad.
A degree (°) is a unit of measurement of an angle. It represents (1/360)th of a full rotation around a point. In simpler terms, a degree is the measure of an angle, with a complete circle being 360°.

A radian is a unit of angular measure in mathematics, particularly in trigonometry. It is defined as, “the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the radius of the circle”. Unlike degrees, which are based on dividing a circle into 360 parts, the radian is inherently related to the circle's geometry and arc length.

fullMarks: For angle conversions, show the conversion factor and the cancellation: multiply degrees by π/180 or radians by 180/π. Keep exact answers in terms of π when asked.
For DMS conversions, show the minutes ÷ 60 and seconds ÷ 3600 parts separately before adding them.
For a sector problem, convert the central angle to radians first, write ℓ = rθ or A = 1/2 × r² × θ, and give the correct final units: cm or cm².
For a right-triangle ratio, identify the opposite side, adjacent side and hypotenuse with respect to the stated angle before substituting values.
For an identity proof, begin with L.H.S. or R.H.S., show one valid algebraic step per line, name the identity used when helpful, and finish by stating that L.H.S. = R.H.S.
For a triangle-solving question, find the remaining acute angle, show the chosen ratio or Pythagoras step, and give every requested side with its unit.
Use exact special-angle values such as √3/2 and 1/2; do not replace them with rounded decimals unless the question asks for an approximation.
mistakes: Using 60 instead of 60 × 60 when converting a decimal degree to seconds. Fix: convert the decimal part of the minutes by multiplying by 60.
Forgetting to change degrees into radians before using ℓ = rθ or A = 1/2 × r² × θ. Fix: convert first and show the radian angle.
Mixing up the opposite and adjacent sides when the reference angle changes. Fix: mark the chosen angle and identify its opposite and adjacent sides again.
Writing sec θ = 1 ÷ sin θ or cosec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ. Fix: sec is reciprocal of cosine; cosec is reciprocal of sine.
Dropping the square when using a Pythagorean identity, such as writing sin θ + cos θ = 1. Fix: keep the squares: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1.
Starting an identity proof by changing both sides at once. Fix: work from one side only until it becomes the other side.
Giving a sector length in square units or a sector area in ordinary units. Fix: arc length uses units such as cm; area uses square units such as cm².
